title: Avoid repeated configuration loading during portfolio assessment
description:
Account-wide portfolio dogfooding showed severe repeated configuration and scorecard lookup work during per-score assessment. The run makes progress, but hundreds of candidates create a long operator wait and noisy logs because shared account/scorecard/configuration context appears to be reloaded repeatedly. Keep this performance work separate from automatic-execution semantics.

Feature: Efficient exhaustive portfolio assessment

Scenario: Reuse frozen portfolio context
  Given exhaustive ranking has frozen the account inventory and evidence window
  When every ranked score is assessed
  Then shared account, scorecard, and configuration context is reused safely
  And the run does not reload identical configuration once per score
  And every score remains assessed with complete coverage

Scenario: Report measurable progress
  Given a large exhaustive portfolio assessment is running
  When assessment advances
  Then aggregate progress and timing are visible to operators
  And logs avoid repeated opaque-identifier and configuration-load noise

Observed sanitized evidence: the first durable ranking milestone required many minutes; a subsequent exhaustive assessment contained hundreds of candidates and repeatedly emitted configuration-load and scorecard-lookup messages. No client identity or score data is recorded here.

Out of scope for the current automatic-mode change: changing ranking metrics, sampling the portfolio, or weakening exhaustive coverage.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Investigation complete. The portfolio loop invokes the generic score-information path for every exact target, which re-resolves an already-opaque scorecard, reloads its full score list, lists score versions, and then loads the champion configuration. Planned outside-in behavior: a single portfolio invocation uses a request-scoped exact-ID configuration reader; it reuses one authenticated client, reads only the requested score and champion configuration, validates scorecard ownership/version ownership, and fails the individual target closed on malformed or unavailable data. Standalone assessment keeps the existing generic fallback. Executable specifications will be added and run red before implementation. No client-specific data is recorded.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Implemented the narrow portfolio-only exact-ID configuration path after running the new direct-read specification red. One portfolio invocation now holds a non-serializable request-scoped authenticated client; each assessment reads only the target score and its champion configuration, validates scorecard and version ownership, and returns incomplete coverage for a malformed or unavailable target. It does not alter ranking evidence, fingerprints, persistence, or public standalone assessment fallback. Added executable coverage for two exact targets using two direct reads and one client, standalone fallback preservation, ownership mismatch fail-closed behavior, and context injection only on portfolio assessment. Focused validation passed: MCP runtime 266 tests; portfolio runner 129 tests; scoped diff check passed. No commit created.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Implemented request-scoped exact-ID assessment reads with active-account ownership validation, frozen-champion consistency checks, malformed champion relationship fail-closed handling, and preserved frozen evidence on target-local failures. Incomplete assessments now remain visible in portfolio reporting but are excluded from semantic diagnosis. Validation: runtime contracts 269 passed; portfolio runner 130 passed; scoped diff check clean.
